findings.claim: mkdir + chmod two-step pattern at all three cache-dir creation sites creates a brief world-accessible window between directory creation and permission restriction.
findings.evidence: scp-policy-check:227-228 (OPA cache_dir), 273-274 (Conftest cache_dir), 367-368 (CACHE_ROOT): all three sites `mkdir -p "$dir"` then `chmod 0700 "$dir"`. None converted to atomic `mkdir -p -m 0700`.
findings.impact: Sub-millisecond window where a same-UID concurrent process can enter the directory and observe or hard-link the binary being installed. Residual defence-in-depth gap.
findings.mitigation: Replace all three two-step patterns with `mkdir -p -m 0700 "$dir"`.

findings.claim: install -m 0755 places trusted binaries world-executable inside the 0700 cache directory, inconsistent with stated least-privilege posture.
findings.impact: If cache directory ACL is bypassed (CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH, admin container, future permission change), binaries are world-executable.

findings.claim: Conftest archive_sha256 verification silently skipped when lockfile field absent; future Renovate bump could silently degrade to binary-only verification.
findings.evidence: scp-policy-check:264: `expected_archive_sha="$(json_lock_field conftest "$platform_key" archive_sha256 2>/dev/null || true)"`. `|| true` silences missing-key exit. Line 287: `if [ -n "$expected_archive_sha" ] && ! verify_file_sha` — check skipped when empty. All four current lockfile entries have archive_sha256 so no active gap.
findings.impact: A 020F Renovate bump PR populating sha256 but omitting archive_sha256 silently loses archive-level verification. MITM at the tarball stage would not be caught.
findings.mitigation: Remove `2>/dev/null || true`; treat missing archive_sha256 as lockfile schema error (SCP-E001 + exit 1). Add explicit `archive_sha256: none` sentinel for single-binary assets.

findings.claim: SCP_FIXTURE_PATH consumed without control-character or traversal validation in the local script; CI workflow has Python + bash guards that the local script lacks.
findings.evidence: scp-policy-check:328: `git diff --name-only "${SCP_BASE_SHA}..${SCP_HEAD_SHA}" -- "${SCP_FIXTURE_PATH:-.}"` — no validation. policy-check.yml:249-258 Python guard (rejects empty, \n, \r, \x00) and bash existence check absent in local script.
findings.impact: SCP_FIXTURE_PATH containing \n injects spurious entries into the changed-files manifest, silently corrupting conftest input. Requires --allow-env-overrides to reach CI-parity mode.
findings.mitigation: Mirror policy-check.yml:249-258 in prepare_changed_files: reject control chars, assert non-default path exists under REPO_ROOT.

findings.claim: Local script performs no Sigstore gh attestation verify on downloaded OPA binary; CI workflow does. Supply-chain assurance diverges between local and CI paths.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml:207: `gh attestation verify "${BIN_DIR}/opa" --repo open-policy-agent/opa`. scp-policy-check download_opa(): no gh attestation verify call present.
findings.impact: Developer operating solely on local workflow is at lower supply-chain assurance than CI. A compromised OPA binary whose SHA256 was committed to the lockfile via a malicious PR passes local verification but is caught by CI Sigstore check.
findings.mitigation: Add `gh attestation verify "$binary_path" --repo open-policy-agent/opa` to download_opa() after install, guarded by `command -v gh` with documented skip-with-warning for offline environments.

findings.claim: SCP_CHANGED_FILES_PATH accepted from environment without check_sensitive_overrides guard, enabling silent local policy-gate bypass. Conftest invocation lacks `--` separator before targets, enabling flag injection from changed-file entries beginning with `-`.
